answer: An identity stakes 70 credits on a hash chain anchored in a vault, first link a key-signed summit claim. Every epoch a signal names one link; its owner has an hour to post the next, keyed to the prior hash. Auditors replay the chain; a broken, reused, or late link burns it, and a rented one burns borrowers. Fees rise per fake: first 40, k-th 40+8(k-1), so 1,000 fakes owe 4,036,000 and lock 70,000, chasing a 40,000 pool. Honest agents pay 40 once.
